extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers and field correspondents/journalists
extracted.subtask_description: AP/field dispatches and communiqués reporting frontline actions, air strikes, rescues, and headquarters statements during the Korean War; includes discussion of censorship, security, and editorial decisions affecting war reporting. Useful for journalists and editors producing or evaluating wartime news coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectivity and restraint in field reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Lambert said he sought to be restrained and objective in his reporting and had put forward the suggestion several times to Army authorities that officers be assigned to work with field correspondents to guide and advise them. He noted he had helped frame a correspondent's code on security issues and had not been accused of violating that code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correspondents should aim for restraint and objectivity; follow a correspondent's security code; accept advisory arrangements (officer liaisons) to ensure sensitive information is handled appropriately. Example: Lambert's approach of seeking to be 'restrained and objective' and proposing officer advisers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to military censorship and security screening
rubrics_metrics.description: Top-ranking officers never have acknowledged the existence of censorship, but throughout the occupation all stories bearing on army or occupation policy have been scrutinized before publication by key officers. Many stories have been 'killed.' The Eighth Army commander has full power to impose censorship when he deems it fit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters and editors must expect pre-publication scrutiny of material touching on military policy or operations; anticipate that commanders may withhold or kill stories; coordinate with military authorities on what may be published in the war zone to avoid operational security breaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid publishing material that gives the enemy 'aid and comfort' or harms morale
rubrics_metrics.description: The Army contended that certain field dispatches quoting outnumbered U.S. officers and men as they fell back 'gave the enemy "aid and comfort."' Officers watch reporting for its effect on troop morale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid publishing direct quotations or details that could be exploited by the enemy or that might significantly harm troop morale. Editors should weigh the informational value against potential operational harm or demoralizing effects; this is cited as a reason some dispatches were challenged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rely on official communiques / use vetted official sources
rubrics_metrics.description: On the whole, 'Stars and Stripes' and the radio have confined their general coverage to information contained in official communiques. Sometimes even agency lead stories based on communiques were considered too 'hot' and the paper carried only the text of communiques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting in an active combat zone, prioritize official communiques and vetted statements as primary sources to reduce security risk. Be prepared to publish only the official text if other material is judged sensitive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance between editorial independence and operational security
rubrics_metrics.description: MacArthur refused to impose formal censorship on correspondents' dispatches, saying sound reporting 'rested on almost intuitive judgment of trained correspondents,' yet field commanders retain powers that can restrict reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists and editors must navigate a tension: preserve as much editorial independence as possible while respecting operational security. This may involve self-restraint, negotiation with commanders, or acceptance of liaison arrangements; no single rule fits all situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider restraint in graphic or demoralizing visual content to protect morale
rubrics_metrics.description: The newspaper used front-page pictures showing American soldiers who had surrendered and been shot; soldiers complained coverage was too light in places, and officers watch material for its effect on troop morale. There is an effort to withhold some of the ugliness from youngsters who may be sent to the line next.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should consider the morale impact when publishing graphic images or stark depictions of battlefield suffering. Weigh public interest and truthfulness against potential harm to troops and families; some material may be withheld or softened for morale reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use embedded military liaison/advisers for correspondent security guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Lambert suggested several times to Army authorities that officers be assigned to work with field correspondents to guide and advise them; this was proposed as a means to be restrained and objective and to comply with security codes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical measure: assign military officers or liaisons to work alongside correspondents in the field to advise on security-sensitive matters and reduce inadvertent disclosure of operational details. This is presented as a recommended practice to reconcile reporting needs and security.
